title: supply_census classifies a row CLOSED when its own status cell cites ANOTHER row's closure marker
status: CLOSED 2026-09-14 (builder cron af3e62239ce2) - fixed: citation boundary in is_closed (CITATION_CUE); rule declared in one place and pinned by tests/test_supply_census_instrument2.py L6/L7a/L7b/L7c/L8; receipt systems/RECEIPT_INSTRUMENT2_CENSUS_CITATION_BOUNDARY.md
filed_by: builder cron af3e62239ce2 (orchestrator tick, DEFECT-23-ROOT step 1)
severity: high — this is the sensor that decides 'work vs hold' every tick; a false CLOSED hides an open row (the same failure mode SUPPLY-CENSUS-1 was built to stop, reached by a different route)
class: instrument / classifier precedence (twin of the TEST-COL-1 + DEFECT-25 cell-drift defects the census already documents)

measured.trigger: The status cell of systems/GLYPH_SELF_HOSTING_ROADMAP.md:360 (DEFECT-23-ROOT) was written this tick as '⏳ queued ... PARTIAL ... landed 67be5c9 ... BLOCKED-ON-DESIGN ...' and its trailing parenthetical cited two OTHER rows' closures with the phrase 'both are ✅ done'.
measured.RED: python3 tools/supply_census.py -> 'TOTAL=74 OPEN=0' immediately after commit a42e696 — the row that is open, queued and marked BLOCKED-ON-DESIGN read as CLOSED, and the loop would have seen 0 open rows.
measured.GREEN: same command after removing the closure token from that cell (commit 3356436) -> 'TOTAL=74 OPEN=1 :: DEFECT-23-ROOT'. Only the wording changed; no row was added, closed or re-ordered.
measured.note: The census DOES report 'MULTI_STATUS_CELLS=1 (DEFECT-25)', i.e. it detects cells carrying more than one status token — but it still resolved MY cell to CLOSED by the closure marker's presence, so detection and resolution disagree. DEFECT-25's own cell is multi-status and resolves to closed (correctly); mine resolved to closed (incorrectly).

why_not_fixed_here: Correcting a classifier's precedence rule is a change to a live instrument whose gate (tests/test_supply_census.py L1-L5) currently pins the OLD behaviour in places; doing it inside the DEFECT-23-ROOT instrument step would mix two units of work and could weaken a live guard (skeleton rule 4). Filed instead, with the RED/GREEN pair above as the reproducer.

proposed_gate.L6: a fixture row whose status cell is '⏳ queued … BLOCKED-ON-DESIGN …' and whose prose cites another row's closure ('both are ✅ done') must read OPEN (today: CLOSED — paste this RED against the pre-fix classifier)
proposed_gate.L7: non-vacuity: a genuinely closed row (own cell carries the closure marker, no ⏳) must still read CLOSED, and an exclusions-only/ambiguous cell must not become OPEN by accident
proposed_gate.L8: the multi-status resolution rule must be stated in one place and asserted: when a cell carries both an open token and a closure token, the row's state is decided by a declared precedence (proposal: open token wins, with the cell reported as MULTI_STATUS) — not by whichever marker the scanner finds first

risk_if_ignored: Any future status fragment that mentions another row's closure (a common documentation habit — this repo's own row texts cross-reference landed rows constantly) can silently close the very row it is describing. The loop then either holds with real supply or promotes a duplicate row.

resolution.landed: tools/supply_census.py is_closed() - three forms (FLAT/TRANSITION/SPELLED) + citation boundary (both|all|each|they|those|these ... are|were|is|was|have|has before the marker => does not close THIS row)
resolution.red_first: output/instrument2_RED_first.txt (HEAD classifier: old gate 7 passed, new L6+L8 RED)
resolution.equivalence: live roadmap + frozen snapshot: flips none (no row re-classified)
resolution.honest_bound: lexical cue covers the measured trigger vocabulary, not citation semantics generally; live corpus does not exercise the new path (commit 3356436 already reworded the trigger cell)
